translationRepairs: s0003 〈（撻不也）〉 is a parenthetical name; the idiomatic “(Tabuye)〉” retains a stray closing book-title mark from the Chinese punctuation, so removing it is a real cleanup.
The same stray 〉 remains in the literal “(Tabuye)〉”; stripping it matches the Chinese parenthetical without inventing or omitting content.
He then ringed the carts into a camp, dismantled the traveling horses to make weapons, and led more than thirty mounted officials and close attendants to form a battle line outside the barrier posts.
He then ringed the carts into a camp, dismantled the cheval-de-frise to make weapons, and led more than thirty mounted officials and close attendants to form a battle line outside the barrier posts.
In 拆行馬，作兵仗 amid ringing carts into a camp and lining up outside 柢枑, 行馬 is a defensive barrier (cheval-de-frise), not traveling horses; the proposed wording corrects that misreading.

Thereupon he ringed the carts into a camp, dismantled the traveling horses, fashioned weapons, and led more than thirty mounted officials and close attendants to form a battle line outside the barrier posts.

Thereupon he ringed the carts into a camp, dismantled the cheval-de-frise, fashioned weapons, and led more than thirty mounted officials and close attendants to form a battle line outside the barrier posts.
The literal likewise renders 行馬 as traveling horses; cheval-de-frise fits 拆行馬…作兵仗 and the surrounding camp and barrier-post context.

The emperor asked about the relative merits of Confucian scholars ancient and modern; his divinatory reply pleased the emperor, and he was made Administrator of Xingzhong Prefecture, then transferred to Military Commissioner of the Shuofang Army.

The emperor asked about the relative merits of Confucian scholars ancient and modern; his extempore reply pleased the emperor, and he was made Administrator of Xingzhong Prefecture, then transferred to Military Commissioner of the Shuofang Army.
占對稱旨 after the emperor’s question on Confucian scholars means an extempore oral reply that pleased him, not a divinatory answer.
